questions.question: In which state is the Kaiga Nuclear Power Project located?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kaiga Nuclear Power Project** is situated in the **Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka**, India.
 
• This nuclear power station is operated by the **Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL)**.
 
• Kaiga is one of India's **major nuclear power plants**, contributing to the country's energy demands through **nuclear technology**.
 
• The Kaiga Nuclear Power Plant consists of **four units**, each with a capacity of **220 MW**, utilizing **Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs)**.
 
• It plays an important role in reducing dependence on fossil fuels and ensuring **sustainable energy production**.
 
• This power station is known for its **eco-friendly operation**, as it significantly reduces carbon emissions compared to conventional energy sources.
 
• The site is located near the **Western Ghats**, a region known for its biodiversity and ecological significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bihar**__

 __
 
• **Bihar** is not home to any major nuclear power plants.
 
• Bihar is known for its historical significance, including places like **Bodh Gaya**, where Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment.
 
• The state is rich in cultural heritage but does not feature nuclear energy infrastructure like Karnataka.
 
 
 
• **Assam**__
 __
 
• **Assam** is renowned for its **oil refineries**, tea plantations, and biodiversity.
 
• However, it does not house any nuclear power plants; its focus is more on conventional and renewable energy sources.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**__
 
 
• **Gujarat** is home to the **Kakrapar Atomic Power Station (KAPS)**, which is a nuclear power plant.
 
• While Gujarat has nuclear energy infrastructure, it is different from the Kaiga Nuclear Power Project located in Karnataka.
 
• Gujarat is known for being an industrial hub and has various energy projects, including **solar and wind energy farms**.

questions.question: As per the Census 1951, the female literacy rate in India was:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**0.0886**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Census 1951**, the **female literacy rate** in India was **8.86% (0.0886).**
 
• The Census of 1951 was the first census conducted after India gained independence in **1947.**
 
• The 1951 Census is significant as it marked the beginning of efforts to assess the population and various socio-economic indicators, including **literacy rates.**
 
• The low female literacy rate highlighted the **gender disparities** and the limited access to education for women during that period.
 
• This data emphasized the need for **government initiatives** to improve education, especially for women, in the years to come.
 
• The literacy rate in subsequent censuses has shown improvement due to efforts such as the **National Literacy Mission** and schemes like **Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao.**
 
• The Constitution of India, under **Article 21A**, guarantees the **right to education**, ensuring free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14 years.
 
• The historical significance of the 1951 Census literacy data reflects the **socio-economic challenges** faced by post-independence India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Literacy Data**__

 __
 
• **Literacy rates** are crucial indicators of a nation's socio-economic development.
 
• They help policymakers frame **education policies** and allocate resources effectively.
 
• The data serves as a benchmark to measure progress in the field of education over time.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of Census 1951**__
 
 
• The Census 1951 was conducted under the leadership of **Registrar General of India**, setting the foundation for future censuses.
 
• It provided valuable insights into the population distribution, literacy rates, and other demographic indicators.

questions.question: Theravada is known as the official religion of which of the following neighbouring countries of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Theravada Buddhism** is the oldest form of Buddhism and is widely practiced in **Sri Lanka**.
 
• It is considered the **official religion of Sri Lanka**, with the majority of the population (around 70%) adhering to it.
 
• The philosophy of Theravada Buddhism is based on the teachings of **Gautama Buddha**, focusing on achieving liberation (Nirvana) through self-discipline and meditation.
 
• Sri Lanka has a rich tradition of Theravada Buddhist practices and institutions, including ancient temples like the **Temple of the Tooth Relic** in Kandy.
 
• The influence of Theravada Buddhism is evident in Sri Lankan art, architecture, and festivals, such as the **Esala Perahera**.
 
• Sri Lanka has also played a significant role in preserving and spreading Theravada Buddhist scriptures, particularly the **Pali Canon**.
 
• The religion has been a fundamental part of Sri Lanka’s identity since the arrival of Buddhism on the island in the **3rd century BCE**, during the reign of King Devanampiya Tissa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Afghanistan**__

 __
 
• Afghanistan is predominantly an **Islamic country**, with the majority of the population following Sunni Islam.
 
• Historically, Buddhism was practiced in Afghanistan, evident from sites like the **Bamiyan Buddhas**, but it largely disappeared after the Islamic conquest.
 
 
 
• **Bangladesh**__
 __
 
• Bangladesh is also a predominantly **Islamic country**, with Islam being the state religion.
 
• A small minority of the population practices Buddhism, primarily the **Theravada tradition**, but it is not the official religion of the country.
 
 
 
• **Pakistan**__
 
 
• Pakistan is an **Islamic Republic**, and Islam is its official religion.
 
• Although Buddhism once thrived in the region during the time of the **Gandhara civilization**, it is no longer widely practiced.

questions.question: Which of the following dance awards is organised by the National Institute of Indian Classical Dance?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Abhinandan Saroja**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Abhinandan Saroja** is a prestigious dance award organised by the **National Institute of Indian Classical Dance**.
 
• This award is specifically focused on recognising and honouring exceptional contributions in the field of **Indian classical dance.**
 
• The **National Institute of Indian Classical Dance** is an organisation dedicated to the preservation, promotion, and development of **traditional Indian dance forms.**
 
• The award signifies the importance of **Abhinaya**, which is the art of expression in classical dance forms, a crucial element in many Indian dance traditions.
 
• Recipients of this award are often individuals who have shown **excellence in performance**, contributed to teaching, or have played a major role in the propagation of **Indian classical dance.**
 
• It includes performances and contributions across various classical dance forms such as **Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Kathakali.**
 
• The award ceremony is often accompanied by performances that celebrate the diversity and richness of **Indian classical dance.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bharata Shastra Nritya Praveena**__

 __
 
• This term refers to a title or recognition given to individuals who excel in the study and practice of **Bharata Shastra**, an ancient text on Indian classical dance and drama.
 
• The **Bharata Shastra**, also known as the **Natyashastra**, is a seminal work by **Bharata Muni** that outlines the principles of Indian classical dance, drama, and music.
 
• However, this is not a specific award associated with the **National Institute of Indian Classical Dance.**
 
 
 
• **Natya Shiromani National**__
 __
 
• **Natya Shiromani** translates to "Crown Jewel of Dance" and may refer to an honorary title or recognition, but it is not specifically linked to the **National Institute of Indian Classical Dance.**
 
• This could denote excellence in dance at a national level but lacks association with the award mentioned in the question.
 
 
 
• **Sanatan Sangeet Sanskriti**__
 
 
• **Sanatan Sangeet Sanskriti** refers to the eternal and traditional heritage of Indian music and dance.
 
• This is not an award but rather a broader concept encompassing the cultural and artistic traditions of **Indian classical music and dance.**

questions.question: How many central banks can a country have?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**One**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **central bank** is a national institution responsible for managing the **currency, monetary policy, and financial stability** of a country.
 
• Most countries have **one central bank** to ensure a centralized authority managing monetary policy and to avoid conflicts in economic strategies.
 
• The central bank acts as a regulator of commercial banks, ensuring the **stability of the banking system**.
 
• In India, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the central bank, established in **1935** under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• Central banks issue **currency**, control inflation, and ensure smooth economic functioning by implementing **monetary policies**.
 
• They play a crucial role in maintaining the **foreign exchange reserve** and stabilizing the national economy in times of crisis.
 
• The central bank serves as the **lender of last resort** to commercial banks during financial distress.
 
• Examples of central banks include the **Federal Reserve** in the United States, the **European Central Bank**, and the **Bank of England**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Four**__

 __
 
• Having multiple central banks in a single country can lead to **confusion and conflicts** in monetary policies.
 
• It would result in lack of **uniformity** in managing inflation, interest rates, and currency stability.
 
 
 
• **Three**__
 __
 
• Similar to having four central banks, having three would create **overlapping functions** and dilute the efficiency of economic management.
 
 
 
• **Two**__
 
 
• Some countries have dual monetary systems for specific reasons, but this is not common as it complicates **policy implementation**.
 
• For example, Hong Kong and Macau both have monetary authorities but operate under special circumstances.

questions.question: What is the rate of movement of tectonic plate boundaries?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1-2 inches per year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tectonic plates** are massive slabs of the Earth's lithosphere that fit together like a puzzle and float on the semi-fluid asthenosphere below.
 
• The **rate of movement** of tectonic plates is generally very slow, measured in terms of inches or centimeters per year.
 
• The typical movement rate of tectonic plate boundaries is approximately **1-2 inches per year**, which equates to about **2.5-5 centimeters per year.**
 
• This movement is caused by **convection currents** in the Earth's mantle, where heat causes the mantle material to flow and drag the plates along.
 
• Such movements are responsible for **earthquakes, volcanic activity, and the formation of mountain ranges** at plate boundaries.
 
• For instance, the **San Andreas Fault** in California is an example of a transform boundary where plates slide past each other at a rate of around 2 inches per year.
 
• Over millions of years, these small movements lead to **significant geological changes**, such as the drifting apart of continents, forming features like the Atlantic Ocean.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **1-2 mm per year**__

 __
 
• This is an **incorrect option** because tectonic plates move at a much faster rate than this.
 
• Movements of only **1-2 mm per year** are more typical for processes like **land subsidence or soil erosion**, not tectonic plates.
 
 
 
• **1-2 meters per year**__
 __
 
• This rate is **too high** and does not correspond to the typical movement of tectonic plates.
 
• Such rapid movement is rare and might only occur during **catastrophic events like landslides or glacier flows**.
 
 
 
• **2-5 km per year**__
 
 
• This is an **unrealistic rate** for tectonic plate movement.
 
• Movements of kilometers per year are associated with **fast-moving objects** like glaciers or ocean currents, not geological plates.

questions.question: Which Rigvedic God is considered an intermediary between God and men?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Agni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agni** is one of the most important deities in the **Rigveda** and is highly revered as the **fire god.**
 
• Agni is considered the **messenger** who carries offerings from humans to the gods.
 
• He serves as an intermediary between **men and divine forces**, connecting the human realm with the spiritual.
 
• The word “Agni” in Sanskrit translates to **fire**, which is central to Vedic rituals and sacrifices.
 
• Agni is often depicted as having two heads, symbolizing his role in both **domestic and sacrificial fires**.
 
• He is invoked in almost all Vedic ceremonies, including **Yajnas (ritual offerings).**
 
• Agni is also associated with **purity, transformation, and illumination**, as fire is seen as a purifier and a force that transforms substances.
 
• In Vedic mythology, Agni is considered one of the **Ashta Vasus** and is regarded as ever-present and immortal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indra**__

 __
 
• **Indra** is known as the **king of gods** and the god of thunder, rain, and war in the Rigveda.
 
• He is associated with the **storm and rain** and is often invoked for his role in defeating the demon **Vritra**, who held back the waters.
 
• Indra is celebrated as a protector and provider of rain, making him crucial for **agriculture** and sustenance.
 
 
 
• **Varuna**__
 __
 
• **Varuna** is the Vedic god of cosmic order, water, and the celestial ocean.
 
• He is associated with the concept of **Rta**, which signifies universal order and truth.
 
• Varuna oversees moral order and is invoked for **forgiveness of sins**.
 
 
 
• **Yama**__
 
 
• **Yama** is the god of death in Vedic mythology and is considered the first mortal to die.
 
• He is associated with the **afterlife** and is believed to guide souls to their destinations after death.
 
• Yama is depicted as a ruler of the **realm of the dead** and plays a role in ensuring justice and moral accountability in life and death.

questions.question: After the decisive battle of Plassey of 1757, who among the following was declared as the Nawab of Bengal by the British?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Mir Jafar Ali Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After the **Battle of Plassey** in **1757**, the British East India Company defeated the forces of **Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah**, marking a decisive turning point in Indian history.
 
• **Mir Jafar Ali Khan**, a former commander in Siraj ud-Daulah’s army, was installed as the **Nawab of Bengal** by the British as a reward for his betrayal during the battle.
 
• Mir Jafar’s installation allowed the British East India Company to gain significant control over **Bengal’s administration and resources**.
 
• The battle and Mir Jafar’s subsequent appointment marked the beginning of the **British political and economic dominance** in India.
 
• Mir Jafar is often regarded as the first puppet ruler in Indian history, as his governance was heavily influenced by the British.
 
• The British exploited Mir Jafar’s position to expand their influence and strengthen their control over **Bengal’s wealth and trade**.
 
• The events following Mir Jafar’s appointment demonstrated the **British strategy of installing rulers who were dependent on their support**, a tactic they continued to use across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mir Qasim**__

 __
 
• **Mir Qasim** was later appointed as the Nawab of Bengal by the British after Mir Jafar, but he rebelled against British interference in his administration.
 
• Mir Qasim moved his capital from **Murshidabad to Monghyr** to establish independence from British control.
 
• His conflict with the British led to the **Battle of Buxar in 1764**, where the British emerged victorious.
 
 
 
• **Mansur Ali Khan**__
 __
 
• **Mansur Ali Khan**, also known as **Wajid Ali Shah**, was the Nawab of Awadh, not Bengal.
 
• He is known for his patronage of **music, dance, and arts**, rather than for significant political events in Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Murshid Quli Khan**__
 
 
• **Murshid Quli Khan** was the first Nawab of Bengal, long before the Battle of Plassey, and he established **Murshidabad** as the capital of Bengal.
 
• He was known for his administrative reforms and efficient tax collection system.

questions.question: Ranjani Hebbar was associated with which of the following fields?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Carnatic Music**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carnatic Music** is one of the two main subgenres of Indian classical music, the other being **Hindustani Music**.
 
• It originated in **South India** and is popular in states like **Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Kerala**.
 
• The main emphasis of Carnatic music is on **vocal music**, and most compositions are written to be sung.
 
• Carnatic music is characterized by its **complex rhythmic patterns (Tala)** and its intricate melodic system (Raga).
 
• Ranjani Hebbar was a **renowned Carnatic vocalist**, known for her soulful renditions and mastery over the rich traditions of Carnatic music.
 
• She trained under some of the most reputed musicians in the field, earning accolades and respect in the **Carnatic music community**.
 
• Key elements of Carnatic music include **Alapana, Pallavi, Niraval, and Kalpana Swara**, which are integral to its structure and presentation.
 
• Carnatic music compositions are often devotional and are written in languages like **Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, and Tamil**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hindustani Music**__

 __
 
• **Hindustani Music** is the other major genre of Indian classical music, primarily practiced in **North India**.
 
• It emphasizes both **instrumental** and **vocal music**.
 
• The compositions often revolve around **ragas**, and the music has influences from Persian and Mughal traditions.
 
• Popular instruments associated with Hindustani music include the **Sitar, Tabla, and Sarod**.
 
 
 
• **Bhajan**__
 __
 
• A **Bhajan** is a devotional song, often based on themes of **spirituality and praise of deities**.
 
• It is a significant form of expression in both **Hindustani and Carnatic music traditions**.
 
• Bhajans are usually sung in local languages and do not follow the complex structure of classical music.
 
 
 
• **Folk Music**__
 
 
• **Folk Music** refers to traditional music that is specific to a region, culture, or community.
 
• It is often passed down orally and reflects the **cultural heritage** of the people.
 
• Folk music is generally simple and focuses on **storytelling, emotions, and daily life themes**.

questions.question: At which of the following places is the tomb of Sher Shah Suri situated?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sasaram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The tomb of **Sher Shah Suri** is located in **Sasaram**, a town in the **Rohtas district of Bihar**, India.
 
• Sher Shah Suri was a prominent ruler of the **Sur Empire** in India, who reigned from 1540 to 1545.
 
• His tomb is an iconic example of **Indo-Islamic architecture** and was built during the 16th century.
 
• The tomb is constructed using **red sandstone** and is situated in the middle of a large water tank, enhancing its aesthetic appeal.
 
• It stands at a height of approximately **122 feet** and is considered one of the finest monuments of medieval India.
 
• The tomb's design features include a **dome, intricate carvings, and chhatris (canopies)** that reflect the architectural brilliance of the era.
 
• The tomb serves as a symbol of the legacy of Sher Shah Suri, who is remembered for his reforms in administration, currency, and infrastructure, including the construction of the **Grand Trunk Road**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rajgir**__

 __
 
• **Rajgir** is a historical town in the **Nalanda district of Bihar**, India.
 
• It was the ancient capital of the kingdom of Magadha and is closely associated with both **Buddhism** and **Jainism**.
 
• Rajgir is renowned for its **hot springs**, the **Vishwa Shanti Stupa**, and its association with Lord Buddha's teachings.
 
• It is not related to Sher Shah Suri's tomb.
 
 
 
• **Sultanpur**__
 __
 
• **Sultanpur** is a city in the **Uttar Pradesh** state of India.
 
• It is known for being a district headquarters but does not have any historical connection to Sher Shah Suri's tomb.
 
 
 
• **Bargaon**__
 
 
• **Bargaon** is a lesser-known place and does not have any significant historical or architectural relevance related to Sher Shah Suri or his tomb.

questions.question: Akbar's first expedition towards Deccan was sent to Ahmednagar under the leadership of Prince Murad and ____________:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan** was a prominent noble and military commander in the court of **Akbar**, the Mughal Emperor.
 
• He was also known for his literary contributions and was a celebrated poet in the **Persian and Hindi** languages.
 
• He was appointed as one of the leaders of Akbar's first expedition towards the **Deccan** to capture Ahmednagar alongside **Prince Murad**.
 
• Abdul Rahim was known for his exceptional **military skills** and was an important advisor to Akbar in campaigns.
 
• He held the title **Khan-i-Khanan**, which means "Lord of Lords," signifying his high status and influence in the Mughal court.
 
• His contributions to the Mughal administration and campaigns played a crucial role in expanding the Mughal Empire's influence in the **Deccan region**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Birbal**__

 __
 
• **Birbal** was one of the **Navratnas** (Nine Jewels) in Akbar's court and a close confidant of the emperor.
 
• He was known for his **wit and wisdom** rather than his military leadership.
 
• Birbal did not take part in Akbar's military expeditions and primarily served as an advisor in administrative and cultural matters.
 
 
 
• **Adham Khan**__
 __
 
• **Adham Khan** was a military general and foster brother of Akbar.
 
• He led initial campaigns during Akbar's reign but was executed for his **misconduct and insubordination** after the Malwa campaign.
 
• Due to his early death, he did not participate in the **Deccan expeditions**.
 
 
 
• **Man Singh**__
 
 
• **Raja Man Singh** was another prominent general in Akbar's court and a trusted ally.
 
• He played a significant role in various campaigns, including those in **Bengal and Kabul**, but was not involved in the first expedition to Ahmednagar.

questions.question: Which of the following Biosphere reserves is located in Uttarakhand?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Nanda Devi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve** is located in the state of **Uttarakhand**, India.
 
• This biosphere reserve is centered around the **Nanda Devi National Park**, which is a UNESCO **World Heritage Site**.
 
• The reserve is known for its **rich biodiversity** and includes a variety of **flora and fauna**, many of which are endemic to the region.
 
• The geographical area of the reserve is characterized by **steep mountain peaks**, deep valleys, and glaciers, including the famous **Nanda Devi Peak**.
 
• The reserve is part of the **Western Himalayan biogeographical zone**, which is crucial for the conservation of various endangered species.
 
• It is home to species such as the **snow leopard**, **Himalayan musk deer**, and various high-altitude plants.
 
• The **Government of India** designated Nanda Devi as a biosphere reserve under its **Man and Biosphere Programme** initiated by UNESCO.
 
• This reserve also plays a significant role in preserving the **cultural heritage** of the indigenous communities residing in the region.

questions.question: Padma Subramanyam, Alarmel Valli, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Anita Ratnam are distinguished practitioners of __________:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the oldest and most popular classical dance forms of **India**.
 
• It originated in **Tamil Nadu** and has deep roots in ancient temple dances performed as a form of devotion.
 
• It is characterized by intricate footwork, graceful movements, and expressive gestures known as **mudras**.
 
• **Padma Subramanyam, Alarmel Valli, Yamini Krishnamurthy, and Anita Ratnam** are renowned practitioners who have made significant contributions to Bharatanatyam.
 
• The dance form is traditionally performed to **Carnatic music** and incorporates storytelling through facial expressions and body movements.
 
• Bharatanatyam is often performed solo and is considered a spiritual offering to the **Hindu gods**, particularly Lord Shiva in his form as **Nataraja**, the cosmic dancer.
 
• This dance form emphasizes rhythm, expression (**abhinaya**), and dramatic storytelling.
 
• The costumes worn during Bharatanatyam performances are colorful and elaborate, often featuring silk sarees, jewelry, and makeup that enhance the dancer's appearance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Odissi**__

 __
 
• **Odissi** is a classical dance form that originated in **Odisha**.
 
• It is known for its **fluid and lyrical movements**, portraying themes of devotion and spirituality.
 
• Odissi has a unique blend of **tribhanga posture** (three bends of the body) and intricate footwork.
 
• The dance is primarily performed to **Odissi music**, which is rich in melody and rhythm.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**__
 __
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical dance form from **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• It combines dance, music, and acting, with performers often enacting stories from **Hindu mythology**.
 
• Kuchipudi is distinct for its use of **speech and dialogue** during performances.
 
• The dance form is performed on a brass plate as part of its unique repertoire.
 
 
 
• **Kathak**__
 
 
• **Kathak** is a classical dance form that originated in **North India**.
 
• It emphasizes intricate footwork, spins, and storytelling through rhythmic movements.
 
• Kathak is performed to both **Hindustani classical music** and devotional themes.
 
• The dance form evolved under both **Hindu** and **Mughal** patronage, incorporating elements of Persian culture.

questions.question: In the year 1930, the Salt Satyagraha was led by who among the following?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Salt Satyagraha**, also known as the **Dandi March**, was initiated by **Mahatma Gandhi** on **March 12, 1930**.
 
• The march began from **Sabarmati Ashram** in Ahmedabad and ended in **Dandi**, a coastal village in Gujarat, covering a distance of about **240 miles**.
 
• This movement was a direct action campaign of tax resistance and nonviolent protest against the **British salt monopoly**.
 
• The protest was symbolic, as it challenged the British-imposed tax on salt, a staple in the diet of every Indian, irrespective of their social or economic status.
 
• It was a crucial part of the **Civil Disobedience Movement**, which aimed to defy British laws and regulations through peaceful means.
 
• The march lasted for **24 days**, during which Gandhi and his followers performed acts of civil disobedience by producing salt from the sea, defying British laws.
 
• This act of defiance inspired millions of Indians to join the movement and resist British authority through nonviolent means.
 
• The Salt Satyagraha is considered a landmark event in India’s struggle for independence and highlighted the power of **nonviolent resistance**.
 
• It also drew international attention to the Indian independence movement, gaining widespread support and admiration globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru**__

 __
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** was the first **Prime Minister of India** and a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He played a significant role in shaping modern India through his vision of a secular and industrialized nation.
 
• Nehru was also known for his emphasis on **scientific temper** and **education**.
 
• Although an active participant in the freedom struggle, he was not the leader of the **Salt Satyagraha**.
 
 
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose**__
 __
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose** was a nationalist leader who advocated for complete independence of India and was the founder of the **Indian National Army (INA)**.
 
• He is known for his famous slogan, **"Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom."**
 
• Bose's approach often differed from Gandhi's nonviolent methods, as he believed in armed struggle to achieve independence.
 
 
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**__
 
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, known as the **Iron Man of India**, played a pivotal role in the unification of India post-independence.
 
• He was a close associate of Gandhi and actively participated in various movements, including the **Bardoli Satyagraha**.
 
• However, he was not the leader of the **Salt Satyagraha**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in 'Liberty' as per the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Trust and hope**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Preamble of the Indian Constitution** mentions "Liberty" as one of its core values.
 
• Under "Liberty," the Preamble specifically ensures freedom of **thought**, **expression**, **belief**, **faith**, and **worship**.
 
• The concept of "Liberty" in the Preamble emphasizes the importance of individual freedom and the ability to express oneself without interference, while respecting the rights of others.
 
• The terms "Trust" and "Hope" are not explicitly mentioned in the Preamble, as they do not form part of the constitutional guarantees or fundamental principles under "Liberty."
 
• The Preamble is a guiding framework for the Constitution, ensuring justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity for all citizens of India.
 
• "Trust" and "Hope" are more abstract ideas and are not directly tied to the constitutional rights ensured by the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Faith and Worship**__

 __
 
• **Faith** and **Worship** are explicitly mentioned in the Preamble under "Liberty."
 
• They represent the freedom to follow one's own religion, belief system, and practices without discrimination.
 
• This aligns with the fundamental right to freedom of religion under **Articles 25-28** of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Thought**__
 __
 
• **Thought** is explicitly mentioned in the Preamble as a part of "Liberty."
 
• It ensures the freedom to think independently and express one's ideas without fear or suppression.
 
• This is closely related to the freedom of speech and expression guaranteed under **Article 19(1)(a)** of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Expression**__
 
 
• **Expression** is another key component of "Liberty" mentioned in the Preamble.
 
• It ensures the right to freely express one's opinions through speech, writing, or any other medium.
 
• This is protected under **Article 19(1)(a)**, ensuring freedom of speech and expression as a fundamental right.

questions.question: Based on the number of chambers in the heart, select the odd one from the following.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Crocodile**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Crocodiles** are unique among reptiles as they have a **four-chambered heart**, similar to mammals and birds.
 
• Their heart consists of two atria and two ventricles, which allows for the **complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood**.
 
• Despite being reptiles, this advanced cardiac structure provides them with better efficiency in **oxygen transportation**, especially important for their semi-aquatic lifestyle.
 
• In contrast, other reptiles like turtles, chameleons, and frogs have a **three-chambered heart**, making the crocodile an outlier.
 
• This adaptation helps crocodiles remain submerged for extended periods by effectively utilizing oxygen stores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Turtle**__

 __
 
• Turtles have a **three-chambered heart**, which consists of two atria and one ventricle.
 
• They are reptiles and share this trait with most other reptiles except crocodiles.
 
• Their heart structure allows for some mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, which is sufficient for their metabolic needs.
 
 
 
• **Chameleon**__
 __
 
• Chameleons, like other reptiles (excluding crocodiles), have a **three-chambered heart**.
 
• They rely on this heart structure to support their cold-blooded physiology.
 
• Chameleons are known for their unique ability to change color and their independently moving eyes, but their cardiac structure is typical of reptiles.
 
 
 
• **Frog**__
 
 
• Frogs, being amphibians, have a **three-chambered heart**, consisting of two atria and one ventricle.
 
• Amphibians like frogs have a circulatory system that allows some mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, which meets their energy demands.
 
• Frogs are poikilothermic (cold-blooded) and their heart structure is well-suited for their dual aquatic and terrestrial lifestyle.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the 11th Fundamental Duty added in the Indian Constitution through the 86th Amendment Act?

• The **86th Amendment Act** of the Indian Constitution was enacted in **2002**.
 
• It added the **11th Fundamental Duty** under **Article 51A**, which states: "It shall be the duty of every citizen of India who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years."
 
• This amendment was introduced along with the insertion of **Article 21A**, which made the provision of free and compulsory education for children between 6 to 14 years a **Fundamental Right**.
 
• The addition of this duty reflects the government's commitment to ensuring universal education and addressing the issue of child literacy.
 
• The amendment aligns with India's efforts to achieve the goals set under the **Right to Education (RTE) Act**, enacted in **2009**.
 
• The concept of **Fundamental Duties** was first introduced in the Indian Constitution through the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**, and the 86th Amendment expanded this list further.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are inspired by the **Soviet Constitution** and aim to promote civic responsibilities and moral obligations among Indian citizens.

• **1976**__

• This amendment added **10 Fundamental Duties** under **Article 51A**.
 
• The duties were inspired by the Constitution of the former **Soviet Union**.

questions.question: What does the term 'deuce' signify in tennis?

options.text: The final point in a game

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A tied score at 40-40**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **tennis**, the term "**deuce**" signifies a tied score of **40-40** during a game.
 
• The scoring system in tennis progresses as **0 (love), 15, 30, and 40**. When both players reach 40, the score is tied and referred to as "**deuce**".
 
• At deuce, a player must win **two consecutive points** to secure the game.
 
• The first point after deuce is called "**advantage**" for the player who wins it. If the same player wins the next point, they win the game; if not, the score returns to deuce.
 
• The term "**deuce**" originates from the French word "**à deux**", meaning "**at two**", which refers to the two points needed to win the game.
 
• Deuce often leads to intense moments in tennis matches, as players need to demonstrate strong **mental focus** and **stamina** to win two consecutive points.
 
• This scoring system adds an element of excitement to the game, especially during critical stages of a match.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **A let**__

 __
 
• A "**let**" occurs during a serve if the ball touches the net but still lands in the correct service box.
 
• The serve is replayed in the case of a let, without penalty to the server.
 
• "Let" is a common occurrence in tennis, ensuring fairness in the game.
 
 
 
• **The final point in a game**__
 __
 
• The final point in a game is not specifically referred to as "**deuce**".
 
• Winning the final point depends on the scoring scenario, such as advantage or match point.
 
 
 
• **A fault in serving**__
 
 
• A "**fault**" occurs when the server fails to deliver the ball into the correct service box.
 
• If two consecutive faults occur, it is called a "**double fault**", and the opponent wins the point.
 
• Faults are common in tennis and players strive to avoid them to maintain their momentum.

questions.question: A regal ceremony in the form of Beating Retreat ceremony on the evening of __________ marks the end of Republic Day celebrations.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**29th January**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Beating Retreat ceremony** is a grand and regal event that signifies the formal conclusion of the **Republic Day celebrations** in India.
 
• It is held annually on the evening of **29th January**, three days after the **Republic Day**, which is celebrated on **26th January**.
 
• The ceremony takes place at the **Vijay Chowk** in New Delhi, against the backdrop of the **Rashtrapati Bhavan**.
 
• The event showcases performances by military bands, including the **Army, Navy, and Air Force bands**, in a synchronized display of music and precision.
 
• During the ceremony, the bands play a variety of tunes, including traditional military marches, patriotic songs, and folk music, creating an aura of pride and solemnity.
 
• The ceremony concludes with the lowering of the **Indian National Flag** and the playing of the national anthem.
 
• The tradition of the Beating Retreat ceremony is believed to have originated from the practice of soldiers returning to their camps at sunset and signaling the end of the day's battle.
 
• The event is a symbol of India's rich **military heritage** and is attended by dignitaries, including the **President of India**, who is the supreme commander of the armed forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (28th January)**:

 
 
• There is no specific significant event associated with **28th January** in the context of Republic Day celebrations in India.
 
 
 
• **Option 2 (27th January)**:
 
 
• While **27th January** is a date during the Republic Day week, it does not mark the conclusion of celebrations or any major related ceremony.
 
 
 
• **Option 4 (26th January)**:
 
 
• **26th January** is celebrated as India's **Republic Day**, commemorating the adoption of the **Constitution of India** in 1950.
 
• The day is marked by a grand parade at **Rajpath**, showcasing India's military prowess, cultural diversity, and achievements.
 
• It is distinct from the Beating Retreat ceremony, which occurs later.
